interpretationCorrections: The first two session cohorts lacked a managed Story checkout. They exercised fallback attachment, despite the original existing-local-session-open label.
Their subprocesses/calls fields count the parent CLI only, not child Node processes. Missing timing counters parsed as zero in the early harness are unavailable metrics, not observed zeros.
The historical managed cohorts below use the corrected managed-checkout fixture. All raw samples, including the 29.9-percent median improvement before final eligibility hardening, remain visible.
Absolute latency drift between cohorts cannot be attributed solely to code changes. Only paired within-cohort comparisons support component gains.

limitations: Fresh processes with warm OS and CLI compile caches are not cold-storage or cold-module-compilation measurements.
Earlier managed source medians improved by 31.4 percent and 29.9 percent; the latter narrowly missed the proposed median threshold and is not rounded into a pass.
Final session coefficients of variation are 7.3 percent (main) and 11.2 percent (candidate); every outlier is retained. A component point target is not a repeatability or general-release guarantee.
Different absolute latencies across cohorts show host variation. Component timings are not predictions for Windows, installed surfaces or native Copilot.
Peak resources, billed usage and complete-Story latency are unavailable, not zero.
Phase-entry, receipt-backed intake and publication relative targets, scale/adjacent journeys and installed macOS/Windows/native Story qualification remain open.
Expanded workers remain disabled. No required test, security admission, independent review, human consent or remote-publication semantics was removed.
